follow-up time: 2 years before and 2 years after protocol introduction
exposure: Neonates receiving delayed cord clamping in the post-protocol period
outcome: Adherence to delayed cord clamping protocol
Blood transfusions in the first week of life
cohort: 427 singleton neonates born at 23-32 weeks of gestation at a large-volume academic center
finding: Implementation of an institutional delayed cord clamping protocol for preterm neonates, followed by continued provider education and quality feedback, led to a progressive increase in delayed cord clamping adherence and was associated with improved neonatal hematologic indices.
